docs.title: ARDesign Converter
docs.text: ARDesign Converter turns supported 3D model files into GLB assets with Draco mesh compression. The ARDesign Server launches the converter in an isolated Docker container for each conversion job.

docs.title: Guides
docs.text: Guide Contents Overview Formats, output, and command-line usage Architecture Import paths, scaling, and compression flow Deployment Docker image build, manual runs, and server integration Maintenance Pinned toolchain and conversion constraints API reference Generated reference for the current Python modules

docs.title: Quick reference
docs.text:
python main.py <input_model_path> [mm|cm|in|m]

The command writes output.glb by default. Set OUTPUT_PATH to select another destination. Run the command inside the converter's configured Python environment; CAD formats also require the FreeCAD runtime and a display server such as xvfb-run.

For the complete container workflow, see Deployment. For API hosting and image rollout, see the ARDesign Server documentation.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
main.py validates the command-line arguments, chooses the output path and scale, and calls utils.convert_file_to_glb. The dispatcher selects either the Blender-only path or the FreeCAD-plus-Blender path based on the input extension.

flowchart TD
    Input[Input model] --> Main[main.py: validate CLI, set environment]
    Main --> Dispatch[utils.convert_file_to_glb]
    Dispatch -->|OBJ, STL, FBX| BlenderImport[Blender import]
    Dispatch -->|GLB, GLTF| Existing[Blender import]
    Dispatch -->|STEP, IGES| FreeCAD[FreeCAD import/export]
    FreeCAD --> Compress[Blender Draco export]
    BlenderImport --> Scale[Scale hierarchy roots to meters]
    Scale --> Compress
    Existing --> Compress
    Compress --> GLB[Compressed output GLB]

docs.title: Conversion paths
docs.text:
• OBJ, STL, FBX: convert_non_cad_formats.py imports the file with Blender, applies the requested scale to hierarchy roots, and exports GLB with Draco compression.
  • GLB, GLTF: Blender imports and re-exports the model to apply the common Draco settings. Existing coordinates are treated as meters, so the scale argument does not transform these inputs.
  • STEP, IGES: convert_cad_formats.py starts FreeCAD's GUI APIs. freecad_converter.py imports and exports the CAD model; Blender then reimports the result and applies scaling and Draco compression.

docs.title: Output and environment
docs.text: main.py sets OUTPUT_PATH (default output.glb) and MODEL_SCALE. The CAD path also passes its input through MODEL_PATH. The ARDesign Server launches the container with a job working directory and collects the generated output file; see its worker integration documentation.

docs.title: Draco settings
docs.text: convert_non_cad_formats.py uses compression level 6 and quantization (16, 12, 20, 12) for position, normal, texture coordinates, and generic attributes. These settings apply to files exported through the shared GLB exporter.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text: The Docker image builds its own Blender and FreeCAD toolchains. It is a Linux image and requires a lengthy native build with network access to the upstream source repositories and package mirrors.

docs.title: Build the image
docs.text:
From the repository root:

docker build --build-arg BUILD_JOBS=2 -t ismayilovh/ardesign-converter:dev .

BUILD_JOBS controls parallel native compilation. Increase it only when the builder has enough memory. The Dockerfile pins Blender to 4.5.3 and FreeCAD to 1.0.0, installs the Blender Python wheel in a Python 3.11 virtual environment, and runs the image under xvfb-run for FreeCAD's GUI APIs.

docs.title: Run the bundled conversion checks
docs.text:
The image's default entrypoint runs test.py against the model files copied into test_models/:

docker run --rm ismayilovh/ardesign-converter:dev

These checks need the full converter image; they are not ordinary host Python unit tests.

docs.title: Convert one model in Docker
docs.text:
Mount an input and output directory and override the image entrypoint so the container runs main.py instead of the bundled test runner:

mkdir -p output
docker run --rm \
  --entrypoint /usr/bin/xvfb-run \
  -e OUTPUT_PATH=/output/output.glb \
  -v "$PWD/test_models:/input:ro" \
  -v "$PWD/output:/output" \
  ismayilovh/ardesign-converter:dev \
  -a /app/converter/venv/bin/python3.11 /app/converter/main.py \
  "/input/living room (obj)/living_room.obj" mm

The example keeps source models read-only and writes the GLB to the mounted output directory. Use xvfb-run for all formats because the CAD path starts FreeCAD GUI APIs, even though the job is headless.

docs.title: ARDesign Server integration
docs.text: The server worker pulls the converter image configured by CONVERTER_IMAGE, starts an ephemeral container for a conversion job, copies input and output files through Docker, and removes the container afterward. The default published image is ismayilovh/ardesign-converter:latest; pin a version tag for a deployment. Follow the ARDesign Server runbook when rolling out a new converter image.

docs.title: Keep toolchain versions aligned
docs.text: The Dockerfile pins Blender to 4.5.3 and FreeCAD to 1.0.0. Changing either version can affect import operators, GLTF export properties, native dependencies, and the produced GLB. Build and exercise the complete container before publishing a changed toolchain.

docs.title: Keep output configuration consistent
docs.text: main.py sets OUTPUT_PATH and MODEL_SCALE; CAD import also uses MODEL_PATH. The server worker expects the output at the path it configures and copies. Keep the command arguments, environment variables, and worker collection logic aligned when changing the CLI.

docs.title: Preserve one shared GLB export path
docs.text: Imported formats use Blender's GLB exporter with Draco compression. GLB and GLTF inputs are re-exported so they receive the same compression settings. Keep format-specific preprocessing separate from the final output path unless a format requires different semantics.

docs.title: Scaling rules
docs.text: The converter scales root objects so parented mesh parts are not transformed twice. GLB and GLTF inputs preserve their authored meter coordinates; other supported formats use the selected mm, cm, in, or m scale. Do not silently apply the scale parameter to native GLB/GLTF without changing that contract.

docs.title: FreeCAD needs a virtual display
docs.text: FreeCAD's import code uses FreeCADGui and ImportGui, so it runs under xvfb-run in the Linux container. STEP and IGES conversion is not supported by a plain host Python installation without the matching FreeCAD runtime and display setup.

docs.title: Test in the production image
docs.text: Blender's bpy wheel and FreeCAD are built specifically for the container. Host Python checks cannot validate those native integrations. Run the bundled container checks and representative model conversions before publishing a new image tag.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The converter accepts one model file and produces a GLB. Blender handles mesh import/export and Draco compression. FreeCAD imports STEP and IGES CAD formats before Blender performs the final compression pass.

docs.title: Supported input formats
docs.text:
Input Extensions Import path Scale handling Wavefront .obj Blender (bpy) Converts the requested unit to meters Stereolithography .stl Blender (bpy) Converts the requested unit to meters Autodesk FBX .fbx Blender (bpy) Converts the requested unit to meters GL Transmission Format .glb, .gltf Blender (bpy) Preserves authored meter coordinates STEP .stp, .step FreeCAD, then Blender Converts the requested unit to meters IGES .igs, .iges FreeCAD, then Blender Converts the requested unit to meters

Unsupported extensions fail with a non-zero status.

docs.title: Command-line interface
docs.text:
python main.py <input_model_path> [mm|cm|in|m]

The scale defaults to meters. OUTPUT_PATH can override the output path; otherwise the converter writes output.glb in its working directory. In the ARDesign Server container flow, the worker arranges a job-specific output location and copies the resulting GLB out of the short-lived converter container.

The Docker image's default entrypoint runs test.py, which iterates the bundled test_models/ cases. To convert a single model in a container, override that entrypoint; see Deployment.

docs.title: FreeCAD bridge
docs.text: The CAD adapter starts FreeCAD's GUI APIs in the virtual display supplied by xvfb-run, imports STEP or IGES files, and exports the imported root objects for Blender's final processing pass. Its executable macro is freecad_converter.py; the launcher is convert_cad_formats.convert_cad.
